_howTo: Radio talks with Walla Walla. Each lesson has two: "start" is typed out on the slip as the lesson opens, and "check" frames the lesson's check: its first line is typed above the check's questions and its last line under the score. In the start talk, each turn has Walla Walla saying "them" and the player picking one of up to three "replies" (none means a plain "Roger. Over."); a reply can have a "back" line, and every reply leads on to the next turn.

turns.them: Harrow, Walla Walla. First rain of the season reached the coast Saturday. Aberdeen says a low a day lined up out to sea now, through April. This week, why all winter and none all summer, and why some of it floods.

replies.say: Something to do with the high?
replies.back: Half of it. The high, and the wind upstairs.

turns.them: Harrow, Walla Walla. Questions. Follow the water.
A week of rain, traced back to the river in the sky. That’s the coast done, Harrow.
